Opening it requires the separate key action. If a player has already moved across after inspecting, return that piece to its previous space and continue from there. Treat the lantern as spent because the inspection still provided information.

feasible_example.text: A lizard carried a borrowed shadow across the burning village square. At the well, a beetle asked to rest beneath it. The lizard refused, saying borrowed things could not be shared. Then a cloud crossed the sun, and both creatures stood comfortably in its shadow. The lizard looked up, embarrassed that the cloud had asked for nothing. When the sun returned, he invited the beetle closer: share the shade.

This separates recognition from recall and gives the difficult answers another deliberate attempt.

feasible_example.text: The Willow Span has held forty winters above the river, carrying market baskets one morning and wedding processions the next. The boards will grow quiet, but the lives that crossed them continue on both banks, joined by the ordinary kindness of a way across.

feasible_example.text: A staircase of cups offers a fragile route toward the locked sky. Read as an unfinished conversation, the cups suggest words carefully arranged but never delivered to their destination. Its force comes from the tension between a path that rises and a destination that refuses entry.
